what: Howmet Aerospace makes engineered metal parts for aircraft: jet engine turbine blades and structural castings, fastening systems that hold airframes together, and forged aluminium wheels for heavy trucks.
customers: Jet engine makers, aircraft manufacturers, defence programmes and commercial truck fleets.
money: turbine blades, vanes and castings for jet engines
specialty fasteners for airframes and engines
moat: Parts qualified for specific engine and aircraft programmes, where requalifying a supplier takes years and regulatory approval.
risks: Demand depends on Boeing and Airbus build rates, which have slipped repeatedly
Commercial truck wheel demand is in a freight downturn
It is concentrated in a narrow set of aerospace programmes
Raw material costs for titanium and nickel alloys fluctuate
opportunities: Engine aftermarket spare parts carry the highest margins and grow with flight hours
Record air traffic forces airlines to maintain older engines, lifting spares demand
Margins have expanded steadily as pricing improved
watch: Engine Products revenue and the aftermarket share within it.
